svg.title: A follower's checkpoint write, gated on whether its place moved
svg.desc: The follower's per-tick hook runs on every poll of the wait loop. It forms a place value from four parts: the stream path, the byte offset after the last delivered line, the stream's device and inode, and the state last reported for each run. That place is compared against the place the current arming last wrote. If the two are equal, nothing is written and the loop returns to polling, so an idle arming leaves the inode and the directory untouched. If they differ, the checkpoint is written atomically, two fsyncs and a rename into the follower directory, and the new place becomes the remembered one.
svg.text: runs once per pass of the wait loop

no temp file, no rename, no directory fsync;
sibling temp file, flush and fsync, rename over the
target, directory fsync — then remember the place
An arming that sits on an unchanged stream writes once, at its first delivered line,
and not again. Measured on the shared home on GPFS, the unconditional form wrote
24 inode changes in 3 seconds of idle arming; the gated form writes none.
